subject.title: fix: block no-auth managed gateway LAN installs

question: Should this PR intentionally block explicit no-auth non-loopback managed Gateway installs before service planning, even though that may make existing invalid service refreshes fail earlier and require operator config repair?
rationale: The patch is functionally clean, but it changes the timing and operator-visible failure point for Gateway auth/bind validation in a managed install path, which repository policy treats as compatibility-sensitive.

options.title: Accept the earlier install block
options.body: Treat explicit no-auth non-loopback managed installs as invalid and stop before service rewrite with the new actionable diagnostic.

options.title: Require fuller managed-service proof
options.body: Ask for a redacted Windows Scheduled Task or equivalent managed-service run before accepting the compatibility change.

options.title: Pause for the broader update question
options.body: Hold this PR if maintainers want proof or repair of the original update-mutation claim before changing install behavior.

recommendation.title: Accept the earlier install block
recommendation.body: Treat explicit no-auth non-loopback managed installs as invalid and stop before service rewrite with the new actionable diagnostic.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle is most strongly tied to Gateway auth hardening and no-auth exposure decisions in the inspected history.
